title: Polynomial-Time Computability of a Bit-String Transformation
statement: Let $R$ be the bit-string transformation that takes a string $D$, extracts the first and second components from its nested pair encoding, drops the first bit of the resulting first component, pairs what remains with the resulting second component, iterates the second-component projection for a number of steps equal to one more than the paired string’s length, and then extracts the first component of the resulting nested pair. There is a deterministic Turing machine with finitely many states and work tapes that computes $R(D)$ on every finite bit string $D$ in at most $C(|D|+1)^c$ steps, for some natural numbers $C$ and $c$.
caveat: The statement asserts existence of a machine and polynomial time bound; the supplied definitions do not give informal meanings for the nested projections and loop-extraction operations, so the construction is summarized rather than fully spelled out.
